the exocrine as well as endocrine functions are affected, leading to malabsorption and impaired glucagon secretion. Malabsorption
causes steatorrhea and may require pancreatic enzyme replacement to avoid marked variability in carbohydrate as well as fat
absorption.
Diabetes medications and other non-nutrient factors that regulate blood glucose
No element of diabetes management exists in a vacuum, so it is essential to consider how dietary therapy interacts with other
elements of glucose regulation and diabetes treatment. Besides glucose-lowering medications, other non-nutrient factors that affect
blood glucose include speciﬁc medications (e.g., glucocorticoids), acute illnesses, and changes in physical activity. Some of these
non-nutrient factors are discussed below.
Insulin
As the two major types of diabetes (type 1 and 2) differ in pathogenesis, so the use of insulin differs for each. In type 1 diabetes the
